To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed two XML based interchange format standards, S-PMIF (Software Performance Model Interchange format) and PMIF 2, that can be used for automatic translation between UML and software performance models and between UML and system performance models.
the SPE process can be used to translate a software design into a software performance model using the S-PMFI format and a system performance models using the PMIF 20 format.

(1) The SPE meta-model can be used to automatically create a software performance model from a UML model; (2) The PMIF 2 can be used to export a software performance model into a system performance model; (3) The PMIF2 can be used as an input to the SPEED tool to generate performance results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of XML interchange formats in the SPE process to facilitate the use of multiple software performance tools in a tool-independent manner.
developing SPE processes and tools that facilitate using a wide variety of tools in a plug and play manner.

defining a common interchange format that can be used for the automated generation of software performance models from UML models, and for the generation of system performance models from software performance models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XML interchange formats are feasible, but that the SPE process still requires some improvements.
the SPE process is an important step in the development of a software system and the XML interchange formats are a valuable contribution to the SPE process.
this work demonstrates the feasibility of the SPE process and the use of XML-based interchange formats to facilitate the use of multiple performance analysis tools.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the SPE process is feasible, and the SPE tools are useful for analyzing software architectures.
the use of XML interchange formats is a viable approach for automating the SPE process.
the XML interchange formats S-PMIF 2 and PMIF 2 have been successfully used to translate an architecture description into software and system performance models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPE process and the XML interchange formats are feasible and can be implemented using existing SPE tools.
XML interchange formats provide an excellent basis for the SPE process.
XML based interchange formats for software and system performance models can be used to automate the SPE process.
